title: Level 3 (Advanced) - A-16
notes:
West leads the ♠Q against 3NT. South has what looks like 9 easy tricks (the ♠A, 2 diamond tricks, and 6 club tricks). The only possible problem is that the clubs may be blocked if the defenders' clubs are split 3-0.

If South wins the spade lead and cashes the ♣A, ♣K, and ♣Q, he will not be able to win more than 4 club tricks when clubs break 3-0. South has a certain method of guarding against this possibility.

South should allow West to hold the opening lead. If West switches, the ♠A will serve as a hand entry to get to South's blocked clubs. When West continues spades, South ducks again. On the third round of spades, South should discard one of dummy's blocking clubs.

The club suit is now unblocked. South can take 6 club tricks no matter how the suit breaks. If the defense switches at trick 3, South will eventually gain the lead. South then cashes 3 rounds of clubs ending in the closed hand. South discards dummy's remaining club on the ♠A and is able to enjoy the long clubs.
